findings.quote: I found the time to return to launch
findings.note: The stone is thrown from the top of the window, so returning to the window's top IS returning to the launch point: step 1 of the correct solution is exactly 2u/g = 1.6 s, the time to return to launch. A student who worked the question correctly could honestly tap this route and be told they went wrong - the misdiagnosis the brief calls harmful.
findings.fix: I used the total up and down time

findings.note: Dividing the bottom speed by g instead of subtracting the 8 m/s already there is applying v = u + at with u taken as zero - the concept applied to the wrong quantity, which the definitions put under application (it would then need a route, e.g. 'I divided the bottom speed by g'). Reading it as a dropped term makes calculation defensible, so this is a boundary and weak only.

notes: Re-derived: 2u/g = 1.6 s, then 5t squared + 8t - 1.8 = 0 gives t = 0.2 s (other root -1.8), and the bottom speed is 10 m/s, so the option-1 (0.8 s), option-2 (1.6 s) and option-3 (1.0 s) entries all reproduce. right_route (I used symmetry for speed at the window) is step 1's insight in student words, 8 words - it is not itself defective; the overlap sits on the wrong side of the menu.
